q1: SELECT A.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(B.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT AS A INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE AS B ON A.EMPLOYEE_ID = B.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY A.PROJECT_ID
q2: SELECT PROJECT_ID, ROUND(SUM(E.EXPERIENCE_YEARS)/COUNT(DISTINCT E.EMPLOYEE_ID),2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT P LEFT JOIN EMPLOYEE E ON P.EMPLOYEE_ID = E.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY PROJECT_ID
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT A.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(B.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT AS A INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE AS B ON A.EMPLOYEE_ID = B.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY A.PROJECT_ID
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT PROJECT_ID, ROUND(SUM(E.EXPERIENCE_YEARS)/COUNT(DISTINCT E.EMPLOYEE_ID),2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT P LEFT JOIN EMPLOYEE E ON P.EMPLOYEE_ID = E.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY PROJECT_ID
counterexample: INSERT INTO EMPLOYEE (EMPLOYEE_ID, NAME, EXPERIENCE_YEARS) VALUES (1, 'Employee1', 5), (2, 'Employee2', 10); INSERT INTO PROJECT (PROJECT_ID, EMPLOYEE_ID) VALUES (101, 1), (101, 1), (101, 2);
explanation: Q1 calculates the average experience years of employees for each project by dividing the total experience years of all employees in the project by the number of employees in the project. Q2, on the other hand, calculates the average experience years by dividing the total experience years of all employees in the project by the number of distinct employees in the project, which can be different from the number of employees if an employee is assigned to the project multiple times.
counterexample_dsp: A project with two employees, where one employee is assigned to the project twice. The total experience years for the project in Q1 will be the sum of the experience years of the two employees, while in Q2, it will be the sum of the experience years of the two employees divided by 2 (the number of distinct employees).
